text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Prime Minister Mart Siimann said after a meeting with Coalition Party chairman and ex-premier Tiit Vaehi that they had agreed on all issues and rumours of a split in the party were untrue.
- A work-group will be formed in the ministry of roads and communications to analyse the results of allowing a 100-kilometre speed limit on some roads as an experiment.
- Among the victims of the Australian landslide last week was an Estonian woman Aino Valgemae.
- Police have two versions of the murder of actor Sulev Luik and are investigating both of them.
- Estonia appreciates the aims of European Union countries to make EU integration a continuing process, President Lennart Meri said at a lecture in Copenhagen.
- 40 artists from 12 countries, from Japan to Mexico, are taking part in the wood sculpture contest "Puu 97".
- U.S. pop band Manhattan Transfer arrived in Tartu for a concert on August 6, but lost eight pieces of baggage.
